lesson_title: Grouping in Pairs: The Sign Trap
hook_text: Half the class fails this ONE step. The minus sign is the trap.
clip_script: Now the second pair — and here stands the trap. Minus b x minus b y. Try positive b: the bracket comes out as minus x minus y. Our first pair produced x plus y. The brackets do not match — dead end. Now try negative b: dividing minus b x by minus b leaves positive x; dividing minus b y by minus b leaves positive y. The signs inside flipped — because dividing by a negative flips signs — and the bracket now reads x plus y. A perfect match. There is the rule: when a pair begins with a minus sign, factor out a negative common factor.
visual_style: Two doors labelled +b and −b: the first opens onto clashing mirrored brackets buzzing red, the second onto identical brackets clicking together in green.
pacing: Build the trap slowly, spring it, then the fix lands fast and clean.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and finish the factorisation yourself.
